initial_container_restore.target: temporary PostgreSQL containers using the source image digests

serving_candidate_recovery.zitadel: The candidate ZITADEL volume was restored from the verified checkpoint after the candidate ZITADEL database entered an invalid-checkpoint/WAL crash loop. The API and login services returned healthy; public discovery returned HTTP 200 with valid TLS and the exact issuer https://auth.kokonut.network.
serving_candidate_recovery.kokonut_intelligence: No checkpoint restore was applied to the candidate Kokonut database. After recovery, the main PostgreSQL service was healthy, SELECT 1 succeeded, and 37 non-system tables were present.

recovery_incident.initial_compose_attempt: A temporary Compose override used incorrect top-level resource keys, so recovery containers mounted the serving candidate's live PostgreSQL volumes. No checkpoint dump was streamed into those containers. They performed PostgreSQL startup/WAL recovery activity before being stopped.
recovery_incident.impact: The ZITADEL database subsequently failed with invalid-checkpoint/WAL errors and crash-looped. The candidate ZITADEL services were stopped to prevent further writes. The initial attempt therefore did not provide isolated recovery evidence.
recovery_incident.preservation_and_resolution: The damaged ZITADEL volume was cloned to kokonut-damaged-zitadel-20261107. The checkpoint was then restored into uniquely named, isolated Compose recovery volumes and verified before the ZITADEL database was restored from that checkpoint. The damaged-volume copy and isolated recovery database volumes remain preserved for investigation; unrelated Docker resources were not pruned.
